gen.title: How doubling and tripling keep the cosine ratio unchanged

steps.label: Introduce smallest triangle
steps.quote: The black triangle is the smallest triangle and has a hypotenuse “h” of length “y” and an adjacent side “a” equal to “x”.
steps.orderHint: Start with the smallest triangle dimensions

steps.label: Define cosine for smallest triangle
steps.quote: For the black triangle, the cosine of “b” is equal to x divided by y.

steps.label: Form triangle by doubling sides
steps.quote: It was formed by doubling the size of sides of the black triangle.

steps.label: Define cosine for doubled triangle
steps.quote: For the red triangle, the cosine of “b” is equal to 2x divided by 2y.

steps.label: Simplify doubled ratio to original
steps.quote: Dividing out the “2’s” gives x divided by y, the same value as the black triangle.

steps.label: Form triangle by tripling sides
steps.quote: It was formed by tripling the size of sides of the black triangle.

steps.label: Define cosine for tripled triangle
steps.quote: For the blue triangle, the cosine of “b” is equal to 3x divided by 3y.
steps.orderHint: Write the new ratio with three

steps.label: Simplify tripled ratio to original
steps.quote: Dividing out the “3’s” gives x divided by y, the same value as the black triangle and the red triangle.
steps.orderHint: Cancel to show the ratio stays the same
